chunks: What al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Muskān, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying:

The wall of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was one qāmah high, so when a cubit of its shadow had passed, he performed the Zuhr prayer, and when two cubits of its shadow had passed, he performed the ʿAsr prayer.

Then he said: Do you know why the one cubit and two cubits were set? I said: No. He said: For the sake of the obligatory prayer; when the time of one cubit and two cubits begins, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.

key_terms.حَائِطُ: the wall used as the reference for measuring shadow
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: one cubit, the measure marking the time for Zuhr
key_terms.ذِرَاعَانِ: two cubits, the measure marking the time for ʿAsr
key_terms.فَيْئِهِ: its returning shadow, used to determine prayer time
key_terms.ٱلنَّافِلَةَ: the supererogatory prayer to be left when the obligatory time enters
key_terms.ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer that takes precedence at its appointed time

ai.seo_question: When should the obligatory Zuhr and ʿAsr prayers be performed in relation to shadow length?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the timing of Zuhr and ʿAsr in relation to the shadow cast by the mosque wall of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also clarifies that the measures of one cubit and two cubits mark the point at which the obligatory prayer takes precedence and the nafilah prayer is left aside.
